question.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}7 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}b \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$

*Hint: The only eigenvalue of the system's matrix is $\lambda =5.$*
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$

We are given that the eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}7-5 & -2 \\ 2 & 3-5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{w}_{1}-2{w}_{2}=1 \\ 2{w}_{1}-2{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the first equation is the same as the second. So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}={w}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=1,b=\frac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=\frac{3}{2}.$
